E-170: E-170 has a shorter fuselage than the E-190 and E-195, visible in fewer cabin windows along the side.

E-170 displays a less elongated, more compact nose profile compared to the CRJ-700 and CRJ-900.
E-170 has a taller and more rounded fuselage cross-section than the narrower, more tapered fuselage of the CRJ-700.
E-170 has a single main landing gear unit per side with two wheels, unlike the CRJ-900’s dual-wheel tandem arrangement.
E-170 has a vertical tail fin with a distinct curved leading edge and a slightly raked top, differing from the straighter, more angular CRJ tail.
E-170 has a forward passenger door located just ahead of the wing leading edge, whereas the E-195 places it further forward.
E-170 has a shorter distance between the nose gear and main gear than the E-190, reflecting its reduced fuselage length.

E-170 has a wing root fairing that blends seamlessly into the fuselage without the pronounced bulge seen on some CRJ-700 variants.

E-190 has wing-mounted engines with circular nacelles and no visible thrust reverser vanes on the outer cowling.
E-190 features a T-tail configuration with a swept horizontal stabilizer mounted at the top of the vertical fin.
E-190 has a moderately swept wing with a clean leading edge and no winglets, unlike later E-Jet E2 variants.
E-190 has a forward passenger door located just ahead of the wing leading edge, positioned closer to the cockpit than on the E-195.
E-190 has a rear passenger door situated just aft of the wing trailing edge, farther forward than the corresponding door on the E-195.
E-190 exhibits a relatively narrow fuselage cross-section consistent with Embraer E-Jet family design, narrower than the CRJ-900.

E-190 features a single-piece, curved dorsal fin blending seamlessly into the vertical stabilizer, unlike the separate, angular dorsal fin on the CRJ-900.
E-190 has a wing root fairing that smoothly transitions into the fuselage without pronounced bulges, unlike the more pronounced root fairings on some CRJ variants.
E-195: E-195 has a longer fuselage than the E-190, resulting in more cabin windows and a more stretched appearance.

E-195 has a straighter, less tapered engine nacelle profile than the Fokker 100.
E-195 has three main cabin doors on the left side, one more than the E-170.
E-195 has a longer forward fuselage section ahead of the wing than the E-190.
E-195 has a wider and more rounded cockpit windshield shape compared to the narrower, flatter windshield of the Fokker 100.
E-195 has a higher-mounted horizontal stabilizer relative to the vertical fin than the CRJ-900’s T-tail arrangement.
E-195 has a more gradual fuselage taper toward the rear than the E-170, emphasizing its length.

Embraer Legacy 600 displays a more stretched and slender fuselage profile than the ERJ 145 regional jet.
Embraer Legacy 600 uses low-bypass turbofan engines with smaller-diameter nacelles than those on the Challenger 600.

Embraer Legacy 600 has a higher-mounted wing relative to the fuselage than the lower-wing configuration of the Challenger 600.

Eurofighter Typhoon uses a single ventral air intake beneath the fuselage, whereas the F-16A/B and F/A-18 each have two lateral intakes.
Eurofighter Typhoon has a short, compact fuselage relative to the longer, more slender fuselage of the Tornado.

F-16A/B has a low-profile, blended wing-body junction without the pronounced wing-fuselage fairings found on the Hawk T1.
